subject.title: Feature Request: Support message recall/edit events to cancel running tasks

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared source-message lifecycle contract for channel edit/delete/recall events, or keep these behaviors as channel-specific plugin features for now?
rationale: Source inspection shows the gap is real, but the durable behavior changes session cancellation, transcript/context semantics, and plugin SDK boundaries across multiple messaging channels.

options.title: Define shared lifecycle contract
options.body: Add the smallest plugin/core contract needed for source message edit/delete/recall events, then let channels implement adapters against that contract.

options.title: Keep channel-specific slices
options.body: Allow Discord, Signal, Telegram, Feishu, and WhatsApp to solve their own event behavior without a shared OpenClaw lifecycle API yet.

options.title: Defer until one channel lands
options.body: Wait for a narrow, proven channel implementation before deciding whether the abstraction should be promoted into shared contracts.

recommendation.title: Define shared lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Add the smallest plugin/core contract needed for source message edit/delete/recall events, then let channels implement adapters against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history spans Discord channel surfaces and inbound context/API boundary refactors.
